items.title: Al Chez interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, February 13, 2019
items.q: I don’t want to sound like Maynard Ferguson

ctx.x: Yes it did, yes it did. So that was a lot of fun. That was a lot of fun. But yeah it’s pretty physical. Everything — it’s one of the reasons why I love playing the trumpet. It goes — it kind of goes through my whole body you know. I feel it. When I play it goes through everything. It goes through the physical aspect, it goes through my brain, it goes through

my soul, it goes through everything, and what comes out, every time I play, is something unique and different. And I embrace that too. I don’t want to really — how do I put this the right way? I don’t want to duplicate anything that I’ve done before because I’ve done that already. You know what I mean? So when I’m playing, every note, every solo, every phrase has its own — a life of its own. And I kind of dig that. You know what I mean? My favorite trumpet player is Louis Armstrong. Not because — well a couple of…

Is your thought process when you’re improvising different if you’re playing sort of a typical jazz tune that has quite a few changes, perhaps one per measure or you know, two per measure, as opposed to soloing on a vamp, like one chord?
